conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: LOCK MODE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.3 2) 'The MULTIPLE phrase shall not be specified for a file described with sequential organization or sequential access mode.' OK. §12.4.5.5.3 1) 'If the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, sequential access is assumed.' OK. DataBinder.cs:1108: `file.LockMode is { Multiple: true } && (file.AccessMode is Sequential || file.IsSequential)` -> COBOLNET1512. The check runs after the clause loop, so clause order does not matter. IsSequential covers an omitted ORGANIZATION (§12.4.5.10.3 GR6), RECORD SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL. probe out/probe/lock-mode-clause/gen.py rejects (COBOLNET1512): f) indexed with ACCESS MODE omitted (sequential by default), h) LINE SEQUENTIAL, k) indexed ACCESS SEQUENTIAL at --std 2002, m) ORGANIZATION omitted. It accepts: a) indexed DYNAMIC, g) relative RANDOM, l) relative DYNAMIC at --std 2014, and j) indexed ACCESS SEQUENTIAL with single `LOCK ON RECORD` (no MULTIPLE, so outside the rule). conformance:negative/lock-mode-multiple-sequential (reject-at 2002 2014 2023) witnesses only the sequential-ORGANIZATION half. No negative covers the sequential-ACCESS-mode half on a keyed file, or the omitted-ACCESS default, so test-ref is empty (test-needed). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause is absent from ISO 1989:1985; it arrives with the 2002 file sharing / record locking facility, D.2.4 / A.4.7; no later change to 12.4.5.9 located)]
rows.rule-text: The MULTIPLE phrase shall not be specified for a file described with sequential organization or sequential access mode.

rows.subject: LOCK MODE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check OK for 12.4.5.9.4 1) a) 'If there is a SHARING clause in that file control entry, no record locks are set ...', 1) b) 1. 'If an OPEN statement ... has a SHARING phrase, no record locks are set ...' and 1) b) 2. '... or specify that the default is no record locking'. Code: when a SELECT has a SHARING clause and no LOCK MODE, EmitSharingRegistration registers FileLockMode.None. A SELECT with neither clause is never registered, so ShareOf gives it ImplementorDefaultShare (FileLockMode.None). LocksEffective returns false on None, and that blocks every acquisition arm (PreflightReadLock, ApplyPostReadLockActions, WriteShared/RewriteShared wantLock). Conflict CHECKS still run for such connectors, which is correct: PB669 (landed) read GR1 as governing SETTING only. The OPEN's SHARING phrase (b) 1.) never writes _connectorShares (the only writer is RegisterSharing at FileRegistry.cs:859), so a clause-less connector opened with a SHARING phrase sets no lock. Probe rt1.cob phase 3: D has no clauses and is opened `OPEN I-O SHARING WITH READ ONLY D`. `READ D WITH LOCK` on record 1 returned 00, and another connector E then read record 1 with '00'. A lock would have made that '51'. Branch a) is covered by conformance:2023/l1_read_lock_mode_governs (leg 1). b) 2. is covered by unit:CobolFileLockTests.PlainConnector_SeesAnothersRecordLock_ButSetsNone_9_1_16. No spec-derived test covers b) 1. and no single test covers all three branches, so test-ref is left empty. The b) 2. default (no record locking) is written down only in FileRegistry's comment and COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md. It is missing from the user documentation docs/CONFORMANCE.md, which is Annex A.1 item 153's obligation (a separate DOC row; see dossier_gaps). kb/Work PB671 (open) owns the '§12.4.5.9 GR1a/b1' mis-citation in LocksEffective. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause is absent from ISO 1989:1985; it arrives with the 2002 file sharing / record locking facility, D.2.4 / A.4.7; no later change to 12.4.5.9 located)]
rows.rule-text: If the LOCK MODE clause is omitted from a file control entry, a) If there is a SHARING clause in that file control entry, no record locks are set by the execution of I-O statements through the associated file connector. b) If there is no SHARING clause in that file control entry, 1\. If an OPEN statement for the associated file connector has a SHARING phrase, no record locks are set by the execution of I-O statements for that opening of the associated file connector. 2\. If an OPEN statement for the associated file connector has no SHARING phrase, the type of record locking for that opening of a shared file associated with that file connector is defined by the implementor. The implementor may define the default in terms of standard LOCK MODE clause syntax, specify another type of record locking as the default, or specify that the default is no record locking. If the default is defined in terms of standard syntax, then the semantics shall be as if that clause had been specified in the file control entry.

rows.subject: LOCK MODE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 2) 'If the processor does not support record locking, record locks have no effect for the associated file connector.' OK. The antecedent is false for this implementation. docs/CONFORMANCE.md claims A.4.7 'File sharing and record locking' (SHARING/LOCK MODE/RETRY on every organization), and the runtime supports record locking on all three organizations (probe rt1.cob: '51' conflicts on relative; the existing goldens pb683_open_sharing_read_only cover sequential/relative/indexed). The rule is therefore satisfied vacuously, and nothing in the processor switches record locking off. FileRegistry's own comment cites GR2 correctly as the clause that would disable the CHECK. No test can witness a vacuous antecedent, so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause is absent from ISO 1989:1985; it arrives with the 2002 file sharing / record locking facility, D.2.4 / A.4.7; no later change to 12.4.5.9 located)]
rows.rule-text: If the processor does not support record locking, record locks have no effect for the associated file connector.

rows.subject: LOCK MODE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 3) 'If a physical file is open in the sharing with no other mode, the LOCK MODE clause has no effect.' OK. LocksEffective returns false when st.Open[name].Sharing == FileSharing.NoOther. That is the ARBITRATED sharing of the opening, so an OPEN SHARING phrase that overrides the clause (§9.1.15) is honoured. Under Table 19 only one connector can hold a NO OTHER opening, so this connector's mode is the physical file's mode. Probe rt1.cob phase 2: C (SHARING WITH NO OTHER, LOCK MODE IS MANUAL WITH LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS) ran 17 `READ C WITH LOCK` and got seventeen '00'. No lock was set, so the GR7 ceiling was never reached. Control C2 has the same clause under SHARING WITH ALL OTHER and got '54' on reads 16 and 17, so the clause really is inert only under NO OTHER. conformance:2002/pb695_lock_mode_optional_words cites GR3 but has no SHARING clause, so it never reaches GR3's antecedent and is not a witness. test-ref is empty (test-needed; probe rt1 phase 2 is the shape). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause is absent from ISO 1989:1985; it arrives with the 2002 file sharing / record locking facility, D.2.4 / A.4.7; no later change to 12.4.5.9 located)]
rows.rule-text: If a physical file is open in the sharing with no other mode, the LOCK MODE clause has no effect. Otherwise, the LOCK MODE clause has the effects described in the General rules that follow.

rows.subject: LOCK MODE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 5) 'Records locks are obtained only when the LOCK phrase is explicitly specified on an I-O statement.' OK. Under MANUAL, ReadSetsRecordLock returns true only for FileRecordLock.WithLock. WriteShared/RewriteShared set wantLock only when phrase == WithLock. Probe rt1.cob phase 1 checks both halves. (i) B (MANUAL) read record 1 with a plain READ and got '00'; A then read record 1 and got '00' (A-READ1-B-MANUAL-NOLOCK), so the unphrased MANUAL READ set no lock. (ii) `READ B WITH LOCK` on record 3 got '00' and A's read of record 3 got '51', so the explicit phrase does lock. Existing goldens witness only half (ii) (pb683_open_sharing_read_only, pb338_read_conflict_position, 2002/file_sharing). None witnesses half (i), so test-ref is empty (test-needed). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause is absent from ISO 1989:1985; it arrives with the 2002 file sharing / record locking facility, D.2.4 / A.4.7; no later change to 12.4.5.9 located)]
rows.rule-text: If the MANUAL phrase is specified, the lock mode is manual. Records locks are obtained only when the LOCK phrase is explicitly specified on an I-O statement.

rows.subject: LOCK MODE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 8) 'The setting of a record lock is part of the operation of an I-O statement.' OK. Every acquisition happens inside the governed verb's own runtime entry (ReadShared/ReadKeyedShared -> ApplyPostReadLockActions; WriteShared/RewriteShared wantLock -> LockRecord), with no separate lock step emitted around the statement. A failure to set a lock (53/54 ceiling) is therefore the statement's own unsuccessful I-O status, pre-flighted before the operation commits (PB338 landed, PreflightReadLock/PreflightNewLock). Probe rt1 C2 shows the READ itself returning '54'. No existing test is aimed at GR8 specifically, so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause is absent from ISO 1989:1985; it arrives with the 2002 file sharing / record locking facility, D.2.4 / A.4.7; no later change to 12.4.5.9 located)]
rows.rule-text: The setting of a record lock is part of the operation of an I-O statement.

rows.subject: Lexical elements
rows.rule-text: The COBOL character space is a separator. Anywhere a space is used as a separator or as part of a separator, more than one space may be used. All spaces immediately following the separators comma, semicolon, or period are considered part of that separator and are not considered to be the separator space.

rows.subject: Lexical elements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Except when appearing in a picture character-string, the COBOL characters right parenthesis and left parenthesis are separators. Except in pseudo-text, parentheses may appear only in balanced pairs ... delimiting subscripts, a list of function or method arguments, a reference modifier, arithmetic or boolean expressions, or conditions.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 4)). Picture exception: PICMODE captures `X(5)`/`9(3)` as one PIC_STRING. Balance/position enforced by the parser: probes probe/lexical-elements/unbalparen.cob `COMPUTE N = (M + 1.` rejected; extraparen.cob `(M + 1))` rejected; parendisp.cob `DISPLAY (A).` rejected; subsp.cob `E (2)` / `E( 3 )` accepted. Pseudo-text exception: replparen.cob `REPLACE ==ZZ(== BY ==DISPLAY ==.` then `ZZ( "OK".` compiles and prints OK. All halves probed. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators)
rows.rule-text: Except when appearing in a picture character-string, the COBOL characters right parenthesis and left parenthesis are separators. Except in pseudo-text, parentheses may appear only in balanced pairs of left and right parentheses delimiting subscripts, a list of function or method arguments, a reference modifier, arithmetic or boolean expressions, or conditions.

rows.subject: Lexical elements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The COBOL character colon, except as part of the invocation operator, is a separator and is required when shown in the general formats.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 7)). COLON/SUB_COLON are single-character tokens (separators — `A(2:3)` with no spaces works); COLONCOLON '::' makes the invocation operator one lexical unit (PB428, landed). Required-when-shown: probe probe/lexical-elements/refmod.cob `A(2:3)`, `A (1 : 2)`, `A( 3 :)` print AAA|AA|AAA; refmodnocolon.cob `A(2 3)` rejected (COBOLNET2096); litclosecolon `"AB":N` rejected where no format shows a colon. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators); the invocation-operator exception applies from 2002 (object orientation)
rows.rule-text: The COBOL character colon, except as part of the invocation operator, is a separator and is required when shown in the general formats.

rows.subject: Lexical elements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The separator space may optionally immediately follow any separator except the opening delimiter of a literal. A space following the opening delimiter of a literal is part of the literal and not a separator.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 9)). STR_BODY takes every character after the opening quote into the literal. Probes: litspaces.cob `MOVE " B" TO A` then `DISPLAY "[" A "]"` prints '[ B   ]' (leading space kept); `A( 3 :)` / `E( 3 )` / `LOWER-CASE( "CD" )` (spaces after '(' ) accepted; replsp.cob `REPLACE == XX == BY == DISPLAY ==.` (space after opening pseudo-text delimiter) prints OK. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators)
rows.rule-text: The separator space may optionally immediately follow any separator except the opening delimiter of a literal. A space following the opening delimiter of a literal is part of the literal and not a separator.

rows.subject: Linkage section
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 13.7.4 "The access to a based data item is described in 13.18.5, BASED clause" -> OK §13.7.4 1)) is a delegation: a BASED linkage item is accessed through its data-address, not through a formal-parameter correspondence. LINKAGE BASED items bind through BindEntries(…, EntrySection.Linkage) into the same forest and the Tier-B BASED machinery (BasedPointerField). Probe gr5b.cob: `01 L-X BASED` group with VALUEs and `01 L-Y BASED PIC X(3)` in LINKAGE of a main program, no USING: ALLOCATE L-X INITIALIZED -> X=ABC42, ALLOCATE L-Y + MOVE -> Y=RST; no SR4 violation raised for the based items (SR4's based exemption). The substantive access rules are §13.18.5's rows. No spec-derived golden dedicated to a BASED linkage item located; test-needed. Probe: out13/probe/linkage-section/gr5b.cob. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (BASED clause, §13.18.5, is 2002+)
rows.rule-text: The access to a based data item is described in 13.18.5, BASED clause.

rows.subject: Linkage section
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 13.7.4 "index-names in the activated and activating source elements always refer to separate indices" -> OK §13.7.4 2)): correspondence per §14.2.3 (positional carriers, LinkageFormal.Position / ICobolProgram.Call), and index-names are NEVER shared. Probe gr2.cob: caller W-T OCCURS 5 INDEXED BY W-IX, SET W-IX TO 3, CALL with the group; callee L-T INDEXED BY L-IX tests L-IX = 3 -> 'SEPARATE', SETs L-IX TO 5 -> CALLEE-ELT=E; back in caller W-T(W-IX) = C (caller index untouched). The correspondence half is the §14.2.3 rows' subject (the NIST IC-series and pb663/pb1009 goldens exercise it). No golden asserts the index-name separation; test-needed. Probe: out13/probe/linkage-section/gr2.cob. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the LINKAGE SECTION exists at every edition; the constant-entry and type-declaration-entry alternatives, function/method/prototype definitions are 2002+ per the clauses they reference) || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Linkage.cs#LinkageFormal; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/ProgramEmitter.cs#(LINKAGE formal carrier emission); src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CallAbi.cs#ICobolProgram.Call
rows.rule-text: The mechanism by which a correspondence is established between the formal parameters and returning items described in the linkage section and data items described in the activating element is described in 14.2.3, General rules of the procedure division. In the case of index-names, no such correspondence is established and index-names in the activated and activating source elements always refer to separate indices.
